subject: Tenant Gatekeeper — onboarding security playbook & cutover window
messages:
From: Diego Fernández <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Acme Identity Team <idm@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant Gatekeeper — onboarding security playbook & cutover window

Hi Tony / Acme Identity team,

Thanks for the sync last week. Attached is the Tenant Gatekeeper onboarding playbook we discussed — it captures the SSO (SAML) wiring, SCIM sync steps, IP allowlist guidance, and the service-account provisioning pattern we recommend for production. High level ask: please review and confirm whether the proposed cutover window (June 10–11, 2027, 01:00–05:00 PDT for final sync) works for your ops team.

Quick notes / action items for Acme:
- Share the CIDR ranges you will allow us to reach your IdP and SCIM endpoints (we've included a template: ip-allowlist-template.csv).
- Create an Okta admin service account (okta-svc@acmehealth.com) and grant the Admin API role for provisioning.
- Confirm SCIM base URL and an API token for pre-provisioning a test tenant.

Internal owners: Marissa will drive scheduling and rollback sequencing; Monica will own SCIM schema mapping and sample user set; Jonas will coordinate observability and alerting hooks.

Attachments: tenant-gatekeeper-playbook.pdf, ip-allowlist-template.csv, service-account-naming.md

If this window is tight, propose two alternate dates (June 3 and June 17) — we prefer the June 10–11 slot but can be flexible.

Thanks,
Diego Fernández
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
https://redwood.ai
From: Tony Rivera <tony.rivera@acmehealth.com>
To: Diego Fernández <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant Gatekeeper — onboarding security playbook & cutover window

Diego — thanks for the playbook. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we lock a window: 

- IP allowlist: we run behind a NAT with a handful of static egress ranges. I can share those but want to confirm whether Redwood needs both API and streaming endpoints whitelisted (yes/no).
- Service accounts: the proposed naming pattern looks fine; can you confirm minimum permissions required on the Okta admin account? We prefer least privilege.
- SCIM: we will not expose SCIM in prod until we’ve run a pre-provision test. Is the pre-provision step destructive in any way?

Also, our security team requests that we exchange the SCIM token via DocuSign or a One-Time-Secret link rather than email.

I can target the June 10–11 window if these items are clarified.

—Tony
Tony Rivera
Identity Engineering Manager, Acme Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernández <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant Gatekeeper — onboarding security playbook & cutover window

Diego / team — I reviewed Tony's questions; suggested responses below that we should send from Diego to Acme. I've also proposed a sequencing table to include in the playbook.

Answers to Tony's bullets (draft for Diego):
- IP allowlist: Redwood requires outbound reachability to two sets of endpoints: the control-plane API endpoints (for tenant provisioning + telemetry) and the runtime ingestion endpoints (for telemetry/metrics). We will provide exact IP ranges; you only need to whitelist the control-plane API for the initial provisioning step. The runtime ingestion endpoints can be whitelisted prior to go-live if your network ops needs a separate maintenance window.
- Service account least-privilege: the Okta admin service account needs these scopes: "Users:Read, Users:Create, Users:Update, Groups:Read" and SCIM provisioning scope. We will include a minimal role manifest in service-account-naming.md.
- SCIM pre-provision: non-destructive if run against the test tenant; the playbook includes a dry-run toggle and a backout procedure. We recommend a staged sync (test user set -> review -> full sync).

Sequencing highlights (to add to playbook):
1) Pre-provision test tenant + dry-run SCIM (June 3)
2) Validation and manual reconciliation (June 4–7)
3) Final cutover — throttled full SCIM sync + SAML switch (June 10 01:00–05:00 PDT)
4) Post-cutover monitoring + rollback window (June 10–11)

I've updated the playbook draft with these items and flagged the role manifest for Monica to confirm. If everyone is aligned I can push the updated PDF to the Drive folder and Diego can share the DocuSign/OTS link for SCIM token exchange.

—Marissa
From: Diego Fernández <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Tony Rivera <tony.rivera@acmehealth.com>, Acme Identity Team <idm@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant Gatekeeper — onboarding security playbook & cutover window

Tony — appreciate the quick questions. Please find the updated playbook attached (tenant-gatekeeper-playbook.pdf) and the role manifest (service-account-naming.md). Key confirmations below: 

- Whitelist requirement: For initial provisioning please whitelist the control-plane IPs only — we list them in ip-allowlist-template.csv. We will call out runtime ingestion IPs separately; those are optional before June 10 but required for post-cutover telemetry.
- Okta service account permission set (least privilege): Users:Read, Users:Create, Users:Update, Groups:Read, SCIM:Provision. Exact manifest attached.
- SCIM dry-run: safe and non-destructive when using the dry-run flag; the playbook includes the exact curl examples we will run during the June 3 test.

Security token transfer: I will send a One-Time-Secret link for the SCIM token and also open a DocuSign envelope for the service-account agreement (link below).

Final ask from Acme ahead of cutover:
- Share your CIDR list in the attached template by EOD June 2.
- Confirm which ops staff will hold the Okta admin keys during the window (names + emails).
- Approve the June 10 01:00–05:00 PDT window or propose alternate.

Doc links and artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1abcDEFghIJKl (playbook + manifests), DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/SOMETHING

Thanks — I will send the OTS link for SCIM token in a separate message.

Diego
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Tony Rivera <tony.rivera@acmehealth.com>
To: Diego Fernández <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Identity Team <idm@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant Gatekeeper — onboarding security playbook & cutover window

Diego / team — this all looks good. We will: 
- Populate the ip-allowlist-template.csv and share by EOD June 2.
- Create okta-svc@acmehealth.com with the requested scopes and grant the token via OTS once you send the link.
- Run a pre-provision dry-run June 3; ops will be available for a 02:00–04:00 PDT test window.

June 10–11 is approved for the final cutover. We will put monitoring on standby and have two engineers on-call during the 01:00–05:00 PDT window.

Thanks,
Tony
Identity Engineering Manager, Acme Health
